title: OnlyBears: An Exploratory Study of Embodiment, Sexuality, Health, and Healthcare among Bear-Identified OnlyFans Creators
summary:
The Bear community is a subculture that developed primarily within gay and queer male communities. “Bear” is used as a self-identification and is often associated with larger, stockier, hairy or bearded bodies and particular expressions of masculinity. However, belonging to the Bear community is based on self-identification; there is no specific body weight, appearance, or other physical characteristic that a person must have in order to identify as a Bear.

OnlyFans is an online platform where content creators can publish their own content and make it available to an audience, including through paid subscriptions. The platform is used for many different types of content, but it is also well known for sexual and erotic content. Creators may use the platform to present their bodies and sexuality, interact with their audience, and earn income from their content.

The “OnlyBears” study explores the experiences of adults who identify with the Bear community and who currently create, or have created within the previous twelve months, sexual or erotic content on OnlyFans.

The study focuses on how content creation may relate to participants’ experiences of their bodies, Bear identity, sexuality, and personal wellbeing. Both positive experiences, such as increased body confidence, self-expression, autonomy, or recognition, and possible challenges, such as audience expectations, stigma, or negotiating personal boundaries, are considered.

The study also explores participants’ experiences with healthcare. Topics may include sexual health, prevention, mental health, body- or weight-related counselling, barriers to healthcare, discrimination, and unmet support needs.

Participation consists of one online interview lasting approximately 60 minutes. With the participant’s consent, the interview is audio-recorded, transcribed in pseudonymised form, and analysed qualitatively. No medical examinations or treatments are performed.

The aim of the study is to improve understanding of the largely understudied experiences of Bear-identified OnlyFans content creators and to generate insights that may support body-affirming, queer-sensitive, and non-stigmatising healthcare.
conditions: Embodiment, sexual health, psychological and social wellbeing, and healthcare experiences among Bear-identified OnlyFans content creators. The study particularly explores perceived relationships between sexual content creation, body image and body acceptance, sexuality, personal wellbeing, health-related self-care, experiences of stigma or discrimination, and potential barriers and support needs in healthcare. No specific disease or medical condition is being investigated.

interventions.name: All study participants are assigned to a single non-interventional study arm.
